summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 20%), COPD, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and long-standing substance use was admitted for acute shortness of breath following five days of medication non-compliance, high salt intake, and crack cocaine use. He reported increased depression and passive suicidal ideation preceding substance use. On admission, he was tachycardic and hypoxemic with bibasilar crackles and a low room air oxygen saturation. Imaging showed chronic interstitial lung disease with possible acute exacerbation. He was diagnosed with chemical pneumonitis superimposed on underlying lung disease, managed with a short course of steroids, bronchodilators, and insulin titration for hyperglycemia. His condition improved with treatment, tachycardia resolved, and oxygenation stabilized. He was discharged to an extended care facility for ongoing medical and psychiatric support, with plans to restart losartan and torsemide after renal function follow-up and to continue close monitoring of blood glucose, weight, and mental health.
